title: Starship rule chapter
description: One chapter of the starship rulebook, kept whole. Unlike every other content type this is prose rather than a record: it is the text a player reads to learn how starship combat, movement, repair and encounter building work, and it is where the tables that no single item owns are printed — power dice by tier, fuel and cargo capacity by size, docking fees. Splitting a chapter into items was considered and rejected: its headings are not a taxonomy, its tables are referenced from the middle of paragraphs, and the sections cross-reference each other by chapter number.

key.description: Stable slug identifying this chapter, derived from its title rather than its number so that inserting a chapter does not change every URL after it.

title.description: Chapter title without its number, as printed in the table of contents: "Generating Encounters", not "Chapter 10: Generating Encounters". The numbered form opens the body, so a page that showed both would repeat itself.

sourceKey.description: Key of the source this chapter belongs to, matching a document of the source content type.

contentSet.description: Whether this belongs to the core rules or to the community expanded-content supplement.

chapterNumber.description: The chapter's own number, which is what fixes reading order and what the chapters use to cross-reference each other. Zero is the introduction. The book's changelog is numbered far above the others so that it sorts last, which is why this is not capped.

readingGroup.description: The heading this passage is read under. Same field, same meaning and same reason as on a rule: thirteen links in a row is a list, and a handful of named groups is a path somebody can see the shape of. Absent means the passage is not on a path.

order.description: Where this passage sits in the site's reading order, lowest first. Editorial, and expected to change; chapterNumber records where it fell in the printed book and is not what the site navigates by.

body.description: The whole chapter as Markdown, headings and tables included. Long — the equipment chapter runs to about forty-eight thousand characters — because a rules chapter that has been cut into pieces is no longer usable as rules.
